title: Pin the herdr wire vocabulary and test it against the server's own schema
description:
Pin the herdr WIRE VOCABULARY in a contract, and prove it against the live
server's own schema instead of a dated comment.

Every string the client sends or switches on today is hand-written and pinned by
nothing. The failure mode is silent: the fake and the client share the same
hand-written strings, so they drift together and the suite stays green.

The vocabularies, with where they live in the lifted client:
- method names (protocol.go:55-84, 15 of them)
- result discriminators (protocol.go:87-107) — the ONE case already caught, by
  decodeTyped (client.go:252-256)
- error codes (protocol.go:111-137). Two drive control flow: CodeAgentPaneBusy
  and CodeAgentPromptStalled (spawn.go:342,404,478). Rename either upstream and
  a healthy worker is reported as a failed spawn.
- agent status words (types.go:9-15), compared as raw strings in at least six
  places. See the strict-decode tick for why this one is the worst.
- event kind strings — TWO parallel vocabularies, underscored (events.go:34-61)
  and dotted (events.go:66-77). `Event.IsOutputMatched` (events.go:270)
  hardcodes "pane_output_matched", a spelling that does not exist yet.
- subscription type names and their scoping (events.go:96-124, 161-187). herdr
  SILENTLY IGNORES unknown fields on a subscription (events.go:136-138), so a
  mis-scoped subscription is accepted and floods. The client's own scoping table
  is correct today and wrong the moment herdr makes a fourth type pane-scoped.
- agent kind values (config/kinds.go:132). Its own comment at kinds.go:251-254
  admits this is NOT the list herdr knows.
- metadata source id and state-label keys (methods.go:412,473-479) — a
  client-side transcription of a server rule, unverified at runtime.

Do:
- Add a vocabulary contract file. `contracts/collect-vocabulary.json` is the
  precedent in this repo; follow its shape.
- Add a drift test that diffs the contract against `herdr api schema --json`.
  It must be skippable when no herdr is present (like the live tests) but MUST
  run in the epic gate when one is, and it must fail on: a vocabulary member the
  contract has that the server does not, and one the server has that the
  contract does not.
- The fake must be generated from, or validated against, the contract — not
  hand-written alongside the client. This is the property that stops the fake
  and the client drifting together.
- Also cover the plugin's `events.on` names if the plugin comes along.

acceptance_criteria: A vocabulary contract pins method names, result discriminators, error codes, agent statuses, both event-kind spellings, subscription types with their scoping, and agent kinds; a drift test diffs it against herdr api schema --json, skips cleanly with no herdr present, and fails on a member present on either side only; the fake is generated from or validated against the contract rather than hand-written beside the client; go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green.
closed_reason: Pinned the herdr wire vocabulary as a live-diffed contract, with internal/herd/wirevocab and its own package tests, verified by mutation, and a clean skip when herdr is off PATH so the package still passes offline on its size pins, relations and provenance. One reporting gap: RESULT-yod.md was written but never got its STATUS line, and the agent stopped answering prompts before it could add one; the report itself is complete and archived. Wave gate green (EXIT=0, reconcile 710s).
